about: Which file and folder paths in a chat message become links. Both Botkins apps test their detector against these cases. A detected path is only a candidate: it becomes a link after the computer says it can show it (artifacts.resolve).
how: For each case, the detector is run on `text`. It must find exactly the entries of `links`, in order: `text` is the exact part of the message that becomes the link, `path` is what the computer is asked about, and `media: true` marks a MEDIA: attachment.
rules: A path is linked when it is absolute: POSIX with at least two parts (/Users/sam), in the home folder (~/notes.md), or Windows with a drive (C:\Users\sam, D:/work).
A bare path starts at the start of the text, after white space, or after an opening bracket or quote, and runs to the next white space.
Punctuation after a bare path belongs to the sentence: . , ; : ! ? ) ] } > and closing quotes are left out of the link. A slash at the end stays (a folder).
A path with spaces is linked only when it is written in quotes or backticks, or is a whole line of a code block. The quotes or backticks are not part of the link.
MEDIA: before a path (bare, or in quotes or backticks, with at most one space between) is an attachment: the link covers MEDIA: and the path.
Inline code is a link only when the code is one whole path. Any other inline code is left alone, with whatever is in it.
In a code block (between ``` or ~~~ lines) a line is a link only when the whole line is one path.

Never linked: web and file URLs, network paths (//host/share, \\host\share), relative paths, a slash inside a word (and/or, 1/2, km/h), a path with a . or .. part, a single-part POSIX path (/model, /tmp), and the target of a Markdown link.
